EXECUTIVE ORDER 10303
Creating an Emergency Board T o I nves­
tigate a D ispute  B etween  C ertain 
Transportation S ystems O perated by 
the S ecretary of the A rmy and C er­
tain of T heir  E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Baltimore &  Ohio Railroad Com­
pany, including Buffalo Division (for­
merly Buffalo, Rochester and Pittsburgh 
Railway) and Buffalo &  Susquehanna 
District, Chicago &  North Western Rail­
way Company, including Chicago, St. 
Paul, »Minneapolis &  Omaha Railway, 
Louisville &  Nashville Railroad Company, 
Terminal Railroad Association of St. 
Louis, and all other carriers represented 
by the Eastern, Western, and Southeast­
ern Carriers’  Conference Committees, 
carriers under Federal management, and 
certain of their employees represented 
by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Fire­
men and Enginemen, a labor organiza­
tion; and
WHEREAS by Executive Order No. 
10155 of August 25,1950, possession, con­
trol, and operation of the transportation 
systems owned or operated by the said 
carriers, together with the transporta-, 
tion systems owned or operated by cer­
tain other carriers, were assumed by the 
President, through the Secretary of the 
Army; and
WHEREAS the said dispute has not 
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS the said dispute threatens, 
in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive certain sections of the country 
of essential transportation service, and 
also threatens to interfere with the op­
eration by the Secretary of the Army of 
transportation systems taken pursuant 
to the said Executive Order No. 10155;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by the Consti­
tution and the laws of the United States, 
including section 10 of the Railway Labor 
Act, as amended (45 U. S. C. 160), and 
subject to the provisions of that section, 
I hereby create a board of three mem­
bers, to be appointed by me, to investi­
gate the said dispute. Nothing in this
order shall be construed to derogate from 
the authority of the Secretary of the 
Army under the said Executive Order No. 
10155.
The Board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
In performing its functions under this 
order the Board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10303 (16 FR 11321; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10303 and signed November 6, 1951. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (subject to that section) to investigate the dispute between certain transportation systems operated by the Secretary of the Army and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order, a sentence that nothing in the order derogates from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order 10155 of August 25, 1950, and a sentence requiring the Board to comply with section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline, the non-derogation sentence and the Defense Production Act compliance sentence are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10303 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between employees and transportation systems operated by the Secretary of the Army). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed. The sentence requiring compliance with section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 is a condition on how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, so no expiry of that statute is shown and none is claimed as an earlier end. Executive Order 10155 of August 25, 1950 is recited as background and as a non-derogation reference; it predates this order and is not an actor affecting it.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute. The Defense Production Act compliance sentence is a condition on the board's performance, not a separate command with its own sunset shown in held evidence. The non-derogation sentence is a rule of construction preserving the Secretary of the Army's authority under EO 10155; it creates no separate duty.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus. The dossier leads naming EO 10155 (and, for EO 10285, EO 10287) are resolved: EO 10155 is recited in this order's text and predates it, and EO 10287 is named only in a Federal Register codification-guide index on the same page as the held text."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10314
C reating  an  E m ergency  B oard  T o I n ­
vestigate  a D isp u t e B e t w e e n th e P a n 
A m erican  W orld  A ir w a y s, I n c., and  
C ertain  o f I ts  E m plo ye e s
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Pan American World Airways, Inc., 
a carrier, and certain of its employees 
represented by the Transport Workers 
Union of America, CIO, a labor organi­
zation; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce, to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniar­
ily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of employees or any car­
rier.'
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
In performing its functions under this 
order the board shall comply with the re­
quirements of section 502 of the Defense 
Production Act of 1950, as amended.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President,, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Pan American World Air­
ways, Inc., or its employees in the con­
ditions out of which the said dispute 
arose.

The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Pan American World Airways, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, CIO, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order, and a sentence requiring the board to comply with section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline, the non-derogation sentence and the Defense Production Act compliance sentence and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10314 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed. The sentence requiring compliance with section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 is a condition on how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, so no expiry of that statute is shown and none is claimed as an earlier end.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute. The Defense Production Act compliance sentence is a condition on the board's performance, not a separate command with its own sunset shown in held evidence.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10319
C reating  an E mergency  B oard T o I nves ­
tigate  a D ispute  B etween  the  N orth ­
west  Airlines , Inc ., and Certain  of Its 
Employees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Northwest Airlines, Inc., a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the International Association of Ma­
chinists, a labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by ifie, to 
investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees,or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
In performing its functions under this 
order the board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense i Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Northwest Airlines, Inc., or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10319 (17 FR 188; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10319 and signed January 4, 1952. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Northwest Airlines, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order, and a sentence requiring the board to comply with section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline, the non-derogation sentence and the Defense Production Act compliance sentence and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10319 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The machine dossier did not locate the revoking provision for this pair; the held text of EO 12553 does contain the row for this order (number followed by a subject line) in the No. Subject table on its page 10, and the enacting sentence precedes the table, so the whole held EO 12553 text is cited as the ending source. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed. The sentence requiring compliance with section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 is a condition on how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, so no expiry of that statute is shown and none is claimed as an earlier end.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute. The Defense Production Act compliance sentence is a condition on the board's performance, not a separate command with its own sunset shown in held evidence.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: the held text of EO 12553 contains no savings or exception clause attached to the revocation list (the enacting provision is a single sentence followed by the table, and the only effective-date or exception wording found anywhere in the order is outside it). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.
